content: The TLX nuclear receptor, also referred to as NR2E1 (Nuclear Receptor Subfamily 2 Group E Member 1), is a protein encoded by the NR2E1 gene in humans. TLX belongs to the nuclear receptor family, which consists of intracellular transcription factors. TLX plays a regulatory role in the expression of another nuclear receptor, RAR (Retinoic Acid Receptor). It is also critical for maintaining normal brain-eye coordination and appears to influence the regulation of aggressive behavior. Adult neural stem cells express the TLX nuclear receptor, and the presence of TLX in these cells is essential for preserving their undifferentiated state. Additionally, TLX is involved in regulating the proliferation of adult neural stem cells. Experimental removal of TLX from the adult mouse brain has been shown to result in a significant reduction in stem cell proliferation and impairments in spatial learning. In the subventricular zone of the adult mouse brain, TLX-positive cells are self-renewing stem cells. Mutation of the TLX gene in the adult mouse brain leads to a complete cessation of neurogenesis in the subventricular zone. Furthermore, TLX is required for the transition of radial glial cells into astrocyte-like neural stem cells.
